content:
- Model consistently overestimates prices in early forecast periods, especially after recent spikes; reduce initial forecast values by 5–10% relative to historical mean.
- Forecast tends to overshoot after sharp price increases; apply a dampening factor (e.g., cap at +15% above recent 7-day average) to prevent runaway growth.
- Model underestimates prices during prolonged downward trends; adjust downward bias by adding 2–3% of the recent 14-day average to forecasted values.
- Forecast exhibits mean reversion bias — overcorrects after sharp moves; apply a smoothing filter (e.g., 3-period moving average) to reduce volatility amplification.
- Model fails to capture short-term reversals near 30-day horizon; add a 1–2 day lag correction by aligning forecast with true outcome from previous day’s 30d window.
- Forecast overreacts to recent low prices; reduce forecasted values by 3–5% if the last 5 days are below 70% of 30-day average.
